recreation_brief: 1. Create a slide with white background and add a thin red border around the entire content area. 2. Place the title 'Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) Curve' in bold red sans-serif font at the top center. 3. Add a yellow circle in the top right corner with the number '28' inside. 4. Add the intro text in blue: 'ROC is a graph showing the performance of a classification model at all classification thresholds.' 5. Add the second intro line in blue: 'This curve plots two parameters: [1] True Positive Rate [2] False Positive Rate'. 6. Add the TPR heading in blue: 'True Positive Rate (TPR) is a synonym for recall and is therefore defined as:' with 'recall' underlined. 7. Draw a red-bordered rectangle on the left containing the equation 'TPR = TP / (TP + FN)' in black math font. 8. Draw a red-bordered rectangle on the right containing 'Correctly Predicted as Positive / ALL Actual Positive Samples' in red, with '(Percentage of correctly retrieved Positive samples)' and '(Best Value is "1")' below it. 9. Add the FPR heading in blue: 'False Positive Rate (FPR) is defined as:'. 10. Draw a red-bordered rectangle on the left containing the equation 'FPR = FP / (FP + TN)' in black math font. 11. Draw a red-bordered rectangle on the right containing 'Incorrectly Predicted as Positive / ALL Actual Negative Samples' in red, with '(Error percentage in samples Predicted as Positive)' and '(Best Value is "0")' below it. 12. Add the closing line in blue at the bottom: 'An ROC curve plots TPR vs. FPR at different classification thresholds.' with 'at different classification thresholds' underlined.
